summaries.demographer: Brittany Bradford is a 38-year-old white, non-Hispanic woman born in Washington, D.C. and raised primarily in Bethesda, Maryland (Q85-Q89, Q97). She is married to Michael Bradford-Reyes, lives in an owned two-bedroom condo in Northwest Washington, D.C. 20007, and has no children or other household members (Q05, Q11-Q14, Q51-Q58, Q84). She has high educational attainment, with a computer science bachelor's degree and graduate business degree, and works in a high-income professional technology role (Q16, Q65, Q72-Q74, Q90). Her life-course profile reflects an upper-middle-class, dual-income, child-free household with strong family ties, civic engagement, and substantial cultural and professional capital (Q01, Q05, Q83).
summaries.behavioral_economist: Brittany is a planner with strong future orientation, using spreadsheets, automated savings, budget categories, habit tracking, and calendar blocks to manage uncertainty and commitments (Q03, Q17, Q57, Q61-Q62). Her choices are motivated by impact, competence, professional growth, and social identity, especially in civic technology and leadership (Q02, Q24, Q65, Q108). She is financially secure but not careless, showing loss aversion around housing, health, job risk, and aging-family obligations while still spending intentionally on travel, dining, and cultural experiences (Q56-Q64, Q83). Peer networks matter to her through professional conferences, tennis, mentoring, and dinner parties, but she resists purely performative status behavior and values implementation over signaling (Q07, Q23-Q30, Q48).
summaries.political_scientist: Brittany is a strong Democrat with high civic participation, voting in general, primary, and local elections and supporting D.C. statehood, voting rights, reproductive rights, LGBTQ rights, climate policy, and a stronger safety net (Q23-Q24, Q95-Q96). Her politics are institutionally oriented: she emphasizes not just policy goals but administration, procurement, data systems, privacy, cybersecurity, and implementation capacity (Q24-Q25). She has been significantly affected by Black Lives Matter and frames race and policing as systemic issues connected to workplaces, housing, education, and public administration (Q26-Q30). Her civic attachment is reinforced by her career in public-sector modernization and mentoring underrepresented youth in coding (Q17, Q24, Q29, Q108).
summaries.psychologist: Brittany presents as highly conscientious, achievement-oriented, analytical, and socially capable, with a strong need for competence, structure, and impact (Q01-Q03, Q15-Q17, Q65). She regulates stress through planning, exercise, mentoring, social support, and calendar boundaries, but she is vulnerable to overcommitment, perfectionism, work-related anxiety, and sleep disruption (Q18, Q43-Q45, Q50). Her identity integrates technical mastery, civic responsibility, cultural curiosity, and relational loyalty, especially to Michael, family, friends, mentees, and high-performing teams (Q05-Q07, Q24, Q47, Q108-Q109). She shows reflective self-awareness: she recognizes privilege, monitors alcohol as a coping risk, and is actively trying to make rest legitimate rather than something earned only after productivity (Q28, Q38, Q43-Q45).
